papers.title: Wavelet-Based Time–Frequency Analysis of Nonlinear Acoustic Wave Propagation in Heterogeneous Media
papers.abstract: Propagation of acoustic waves in a heterogeneous media, layered geology or composite structure, is a big challenge because it becomes difficult to analyse it exactly. The conventional Fourier techniques do not sufficiently represent transient and localised processes of nonlinearities. In this work an analysis framework of wavelets-based time-frequency analysis is revealed with the object of the inquiry of nonlinear waves of acoustics in non-homogeneous media. The method uses adaptive wavelet transforms that are used together with numerical solutions of the nonlinear acoustic wave equation that allows a high degree of spatial localization of harmonic generation, shock formation and scattering capacities. Spatial discretization is done using finite-differences schemes whereas multiresolution decomposition in time signals is done using wavelet packets. The outcome of the simulation of composite layered structures has shown that there are frequency shifts and nonlinear effects that are localised and are not considered by the traditional analysis. An original aspect of the proposed research is in its synergic approach combined with computational acoustics where wavelet analytic provides a less holistic view of the nonlinear wave phenomena. Its practical uses are in nondestructive testing of composite materials, analysis of seismic waves in geophysics, and prediction of performance of acoustic device under nonlinear operation. This framework allows the computational acoustics to increase diagnostic power through the reconciliation of high level mathematical tools with wave propagation physics.

papers.title: Computational Framework for Urban Acoustic Wave Propagation and Noise Mapping Using GPU Acceleration
papers.abstract: The acoustic environment in a city is complicated because of irregular construction geometries, changing traffic sources, and the environment. Conventional noise mapping methods, which are usually founded on simplified propagation laws, do not have the accuracy to serve well at analysing urban soundscape. The present paper presents a computation model based on a GPU architecture of urban acoustic waves propagation and noise mapping on a large scale. The scheme uses finite-differentiated time-domain (FDTD) algorithms with perfectly matched layers in order to reduce artificial reflections. Using the parallelism of graphic cards, the system can simulate the dispersion of sound in urban areas with a distance of kilometres in real-time. Comparison to in-situ measurements of noises in traffic metropolitan areas demonstrates a high level of improvement in predictive accuracy over more traditional methods based on ISO. The uniqueness of the work is the high-resolution of FDTD acoustics that is applied in conjunction with the use of a computer with a high level of acceleration, allowing a city scale prediction of noise, without excessive calculations that force inexpensive computing. The framework helps urban planners and policymakers to evaluate exposure to noise on the ground in a dynamic, mitigation control policies like a noise barrier or a green wall, and optimal urban planning policy to complement livability. The study will help in the development of the computational acoustics of urban environment, which is a sustainable objective in the application of smart cities.
